hints.title: Three-Term Summation Obstacle
hints.text: The Tribonacci sequence defines each term as the sum of the preceding three terms. How can maintaining a sliding triplet of numbers advance the sequence in constant space?

hints.title: Three-State Shift Invariant
hints.text: T(n) is determined solely by T(n-1), T(n-2), and T(n-3). Keeping three scalar registers provides all information needed to generate the next term.

hints.title: Triplet Window Sliding Procedure
hints.text: If n is 0 return 0, and if n is 1 or 2 return 1. Initialize three variables a = 0, b = 1, c = 1. Loop from 3 to n, computing the sum of all three, shifting a to b, b to c, and c to the sum. Return c.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: index of the Tribonacci term (0 <= N <= 37)
complexity.notes: Performs N - 2 iterations with three integer registers.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Ternary recursion creates O(3^N) calls causing timeout.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Extending the 2-variable Fibonacci pattern to 3 variables cleanly.
